policies.description: Inert raster image evidence/reference assets under docs/ -- cannot carry dispatch/approval/authority logic, so a path-substring hit on an authority-sounding directory name (e.g. "reference-evidence") is a naming coincidence, not a real authority signal.
notes: eligible_target/target_field are null and auto_registration_allowed is false because these assets need no catalog node at all -- classify_new_sources() already treats *.png/*.jpg/etc as WARNING (never blocking) for any path via extension, not just docs/. This policy exists to make that decision explicit/reusable rather than only implicit in the classifier, per RECONCILIATION.md section B.

policies.description: F15 staging verification boundary -- exact-file policy, not a scripts/verify_*_staging.py catch-all. Verification CLASS (bounded, manually-invoked, *_STAGING_NON_PRODUCTION-gated) is reusable, but registration OWNER/TARGET is domain-specific and must never be inferred from the shared verify_*_staging.py naming convention alone.
notes: Requires decision.f15_staging_verification_artifact to actually be a loaded catalog node before reconcile() will route a match here into auto_maintenance_sources -- until that node exists (e.g. before PR #628 merges), a match falls to the decision queue with an explicit 'target does not exist yet' note instead of being silently treated as safe.

policies.description: Bounded staging verification scripts for the specific approval-callback bug family they were written for -- owned by the Approvals/ActionContracts layer, the same layer their subject bugs live in.
notes: Named family, not a scripts/verify_*_staging.py wildcard: these two files are individually named because they were individually reviewed and assigned to layer.approvals. A new verify_bugNNN_staging.py for a different bug is NOT assumed to belong here -- it falls to OWNER_DECISION_REQUIRED with no policy match until an owner extends this list or adds a new family policy.

policies.description: TC8/TC9 staging verification scripts -- owned by the Turn Coordinator layer.
notes: Both paths are already registered today (layer.turn_coordinator.test_paths and layer.approvals.test_paths), so this policy is precedent/traceability documentation, not an active registration path in practice -- classify_new_sources() already excludes registered paths before reconcile ever sees them.

policies.description: Test-fixture/repo-stub helper files whose name does not start with test_ (so the generic test-file heuristic misses them) but which exist purely to support another suite's fixtures.
notes: Matches the tc8_test_repo_stub.py precedent (registered under layer.approvals/layer.turn_coordinator test_paths). eligible_target/target_field are left null and auto_registration_allowed false because, unlike the other policies, this class has no single owning layer -- which suite(s) a new stub supports is still a per-file judgment call; this policy only guarantees the file is never escalated to STOP on an authority-term coincidence and is never treated as an unknown-role REVIEW_REQUIRED runtime source.

policies.description: Generic, stateless, prop-driven TMA presentational components with no fetch/API/state/side effects.
notes: auto_registration_allowed is false: a new file matching this path still needs a human to confirm it is actually pure/stateless (no fetch/API/state) before folding it in -- the pattern narrows *where* to look, it does not itself prove the file has no side effects. Reconcile still routes a match here to the decision queue, but pre-labelled with the applicable policy and target node so the owner decision is a one-line confirmation, not a fresh investigation.

policies.description: A specific, named module consumed by callers in more than one existing catalog layer, with no single layer that legitimately owns all of them.
notes: Deliberately an exact-path policy, not a wildcard: "consumed by more than one layer with no single legitimate owner" is a per-file semantic fact that cannot be safely generalized to a directory or naming pattern. A different file making the same claim still requires a fresh OWNER_DECISION.

decision.business_domain_vocabulary does not exist as a catalog node yet on any branch as of this policy's authoring -- until it is created, reconcile() routes a domain_utils.py match to the decision queue with a 'target does not exist yet' note rather than silently claiming AUTO.

policies.description: Standalone, manually-invoked offline tools that self-declare (or are otherwise established to be) outside the live SCOREBOS runtime path -- research harnesses, one-off CSV/contact-merge utilities.
notes: contact_merge.py and scripts/classify_contacts_for_airtable.py are pre-existing files of this class (both predate every current catalog anchor commit, so neither has ever appeared as a blocking new_source) -- listed here so a future rename/move/copy of either is still recognized under this bucket instead of re-litigating 'is this a standalone offline tool' from scratch.

decision.offline_research_support_tool is introduced by PR #628, not by this branch -- until that PR merges and this branch is rebased onto it, a match here falls to the decision queue with a 'target does not exist yet' note.

policies.description: Read-only, curated catalog of approved external tools/resources and their recommendation metadata -- explicitly not the internal execution Tool Registry, cannot dispatch or execute, cannot grant ActionGateway/tool-execution authority.
notes: authority is true because this file IS the source of truth for which external tools are approved for recommendation (a real, narrow authority) -- but that authority is explicitly scoped away from tool_registry.py's internal-execution authority, per decision.external_business_tool_recommendation_catalog's source_of_truth.precedence.

Split from its test file into a separate policy (EXTERNAL_RECOMMENDATION_CATALOG_TEST) because the two register into different target_field values (code_paths vs test_paths) -- one policy cannot declare two target fields, and target_field is never inferred from a test_/non-test_ filename convention.

decision.external_business_tool_recommendation_catalog is introduced by PR #628, not by this branch -- until that PR merges and this branch is rebased onto it, a match here falls to the decision queue with a 'target does not exist yet' note.

policies.description: Test suite for business_tool_registry.py -- same authority boundary as EXTERNAL_RECOMMENDATION_CATALOG, registered into test_paths instead of code_paths.
notes: See EXTERNAL_RECOMMENDATION_CATALOG for why this is a separate policy rather than a second pattern on the same one.

policies.description: Approved External Execution runtime boundary, durable job repository, PostgreSQL poll lease repository, and its exact migration. Owned by the Approvals/execution layer; this registration does not change ActionContract lifecycle authority or enable external execution.
notes: Owner-approved exact-path registration under layer.approvals. The boundary owns External Execution submission/poll coordination; ActionContracts remain approval lifecycle authority, Airtable remains job-state authority, and PostgreSQL remains transient lease ownership only.

OWNER DECISION (MPT Phase 2B): core/mpt_runtime_policy.py is an approved bounded policy source for the existing MoneyPrinterTurbo adapter path. It centralizes concurrency, daily ceiling, timeout, proven Render Standard 2 GiB runtime profile, bounded evidence, and resource-limit classification; it is not a parallel runtime, source of truth, execution path, or architecture replacement.
